subject: SLA amendment request — uptime target & monthly credit cap
messages:
From: Sarah Wells <sarah.wells@greenstack.io>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@greenstack.io>, Legal <legal@greenstack.io>
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Request: SLA amendment — uptime target & monthly credit cap

Hi Aditya,

Thanks again for the demo last week. GreenStack is excited about the performance footprint Redwood showed, but before procurement can sign we need two fairly material adjustments to your standard SLA template. Our legal and finance teams raised these points as blockers: 

1) Uptime target: your standard hosted uptime of 99.9% is below what a subset of our customers require for compliance. We need to propose 99.95% for the production-critical endpoints specified in section 2 of the attached SOW.

2) Monthly credit cap: we need a hard cap on service credits tied to monthly spend. Our charter limits our exposure to no more than 50% of monthly recurring charges for a single service. We ask that the template include a 50% monthly cap for credits (vs. unlimited or a full-month credit).

We understand these are exceptions to your standard terms. To help speed review, I attached a short note that calls out the exact clauses we’re asking to change (GreenStack_SLA_ask_20270402.pdf).

If these asks are unacceptable we’re open to a compromise (e.g., 99.92% uptime with a 100% cap) — but please tell us what you can commit to so we can move to signatures. We’d like to close this by end of next week.

Thanks,
Sarah Wells
Head of Procurement, GreenStack
procurement@greenstack.io

Attachment: GreenStack_SLA_ask_20270402.pdf (1 page)
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Wells <sarah.wells@greenstack.io>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Legal <legal@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 03 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: SLA amendment — uptime target & monthly credit cap

Hi Sarah — really appreciate the clear note and the timeline. I’m looping in our contracts and finance leads (cc’d) so we can give a firm counterproposal. Quick thoughts:

- Redwood’s standard hosted SLA is 99.9% for broadly scoped endpoints. We can accommodate a tighter production SLA for pinned endpoints but it changes the operational profile and has cost implications.

- On credits: we generally avoid hard caps below committed spend, because credits are the primary warranty remedy for availability regressions. That said, we can propose a single-month cap tied to invoice value as a compromise.

Attached is a short counterproposal I’ll use as the basis for internal approval. Proposed points (high-level):
  * Offer 99.92% uptime for the named production endpoints (region: us-west).
  * Monthly credit cap = 100% of the monthly invoice for the Redwood services covered in the SOW.
  * Scheduled maintenance carveouts: up to 6 hours/month (scheduled in advance with 72 hours notice).
  * Latency incidents: preserve ability to assess credits only for availability windows; we will not grant latency-based credits unless latency causes request failures above a threshold we can instrument.

If that’s acceptable as a starting point, I’ll request an exception approval from my manager and contracts. If you need 99.95% and 50% cap, I’ll surface that as an escalation request and flag the added commercial implications.

I’ve attached the draft counterproposal for your review. I’ll follow up with the internal thread to get sign-off.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.com

Attachment: redwood-counterproposal-20270403.docx (changes tracked)
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 03 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Request: SLA amendment — GreenStack asks — need approval for exception

Folks — forwarding GreenStack’s request and my proposed counter (attached). TL;DR: GreenStack wants 99.95% and a 50% monthly credit cap (their internal constraint). I’d like permission to offer the compromise below to close the deal quickly:

Proposed exception to seek approval for: 
- Production uptime: 99.92% (region us-west) for the endpoints named in SOW.
- Monthly credit cap: 100% of the monthly invoice for affected services (single-month cap).
- Scheduled maintenance carveout: up to 8 hours/month (we’ll attempt 6, asking for 8 allows a buffer).
- Latency-based credits: keep narrow — only for hard availability failures; don’t accept open-ended latency credits.

Commercial impact notes: 99.95% would materially increase operational on-call and reserved capacity; 50% cap reduces customer protection and increases risk on our side. The 100% cap is our middle ground.

Can you confirm whether we can offer the above? If yes I’ll send the counter and request DocuSign. I included a short internal summary as an attachment.

Thanks — Aditya

Attachment: redwood-internal-summary-20270403.txt
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 03 Apr 2027 14:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: SLA amendment — GreenStack asks — need approval for exception

Aditya — ok to move forward with a constrained exception, with these edits: 
- Accept 99.92% for the named production endpoints.
- Monthly credit cap: yes, 100% of the monthly invoice (single-month cap).
- Scheduled maintenance carveout: reduce to 6 hours/month (we can offer 6, not 8). Schedule must be agreed at least 72 hours in advance.
- Latency: do not accept latency-based credits beyond availability failures.

Two asks from my side: 1) add a clause that we can convert the priority queue for these endpoints to dedicated capacity (cost pass-through) if uptime regressions exceed thresholds for 2 consecutive months — creates an operational remediation ladder; 2) log the exception in HubSpot and tag the deal as SLA-exception-approved.

If that sounds good, send the counter to GreenStack and include legal on the outgoing email.

—Marissa
VP, Sales Operations
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Wells <sarah.wells@greenstack.io>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Legal <legal@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 06 Apr 2027 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Final counterproposal: Uptime & monthly credit cap (GreenStack)

Hi Sarah — thanks for your patience. Following an internal review we can move forward with a constrained exception on the SLA for the endpoints identified in your SOW. Summary of the counterproposal Redwood can commit to: 

1) Uptime: 99.92% monthly uptime for the named production endpoints (region: us-west).
2) Monthly credit cap: single-month credit cap equal to 100% of the monthly invoice for the Redwood services covered in the SOW.
3) Scheduled maintenance carveout: up to 6 hours/month (scheduled in advance with at least 72 hours notice).
4) Latency: credits remain tied to availability (request failures); we will not provide credits for elevated latency alone unless it causes measurable error rates that meet the availability threshold in the SLA.
5) Operational remediation ladder: if uptime regressions cross the SLA threshold for 2 consecutive months, we reserve the right to require conversion of the endpoints to a dedicated capacity configuration (cost pass-through), plus a joint remediation plan.

I’ve attached the redlined counterproposal and pulled the DocuSign link for the amendment. If that looks good, please confirm and we’ll route for signatures. We can also accept a short addendum if your legal team needs slightly different phrasing for the credit cap clause; markups are fine.

DocuSign: https://docusign.example/links/abc123
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/GS-2027-07

Attachment: redwood-counterproposal-20270404.docx

Best,
